subject: biology
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: As temperature increases up to the optimum, the rate of an enzyme-controlled reaction:
options: Increases because particles collide more often with more energy
questions.explain: Up to the optimum, higher temperature increases kinetic energy and collision frequency, raising the rate.

questions.q: What is the main role of the stomach in digestion?
options: Produces hydrochloric acid and protease to begin protein digestion
questions.explain: The stomach secretes hydrochloric acid and the protease pepsin to start digesting protein.

questions.q: What colour change shows a positive result when iodine solution is added to a food containing starch?
questions.explain: Iodine solution turns from orange-brown to blue-black in the presence of starch.

questions.q: Lipase digests lipids (fats) into which products?
questions.explain: Lipase breaks lipids down into fatty acids and glycerol.
Bile is produced in the liver and then stored in the gall bladder.

questions.q: Which statement about bile is correct?
options: It is made in the pancreas
It breaks protein into amino acids
It is an enzyme that digests fat
It emulsifies fats and neutralises stomach acid
questions.explain: Bile is not an enzyme; it emulsifies fat and is alkaline so it neutralises acid from the stomach.

questions.q: The 'lock and key' model explains that an enzyme:
options: Has an active site with a specific shape that fits a particular substrate
questions.explain: The active site has a complementary shape to its specific substrate, like a key fitting a lock.

questions.q: Why does a very high or very low pH usually stop an enzyme working?
options: It changes the shape of the active site, denaturing the enzyme
It gives the enzyme more energy
It turns the enzyme into a product
questions.explain: Extreme pH alters the active site's shape (denaturation) so the substrate no longer fits.

questions.q: A student says 'boiling the enzyme killed it.' What is the correct scientific statement?
options: The enzyme was killed and is now dead
The enzyme turned into a substrate
The enzyme used up its energy
The enzyme was denatured, changing the active site's shape
questions.explain: Enzymes are not living, so they cannot be killed; high temperature denatures them.

questions.q: What does protease break protein down into?
questions.explain: Protease enzymes digest proteins into amino acids.

questions.q: Why does the stomach produce hydrochloric acid?
options: To provide the optimum pH for stomach protease and kill bacteria
questions.explain: The acidic conditions kill pathogens and give the right pH for the protease in the stomach to work.

options: Biological catalysts that speed up reactions
questions.explain: Enzymes are biological catalysts; they speed up reactions and are not used up.
